data.question_title:
In my village a fair is held every year. If I happen to be in my village on the day of the fair, I make it a point to attend it. I attend it this year and I retain very happy impressions of all the sights and sounds that I enjoyed.

It was a cloudy day and so I went to the fair on foot. On the way I saw a number of villagers, dressed in their best clothes, going to the fair. They appeared to be in high spirits. They were accompanied by their children who wore turbans of dark red colour. As I approached the fair, I heard a mingling noise. A number of booths and stalls constituting the bazaars of the fair met my eyes. Every villager was buying sweets. The children seemed to be going crazy about sweets.

In the midst of a vast crowd I saw a rope-dancer amusing the audience by keeping his balance wonderfully on the rope. The villagers clapped their hands. A little further I saw the inevitable juggler. He was accompanied by two children; one of whom played on the flute, while the other beat a small drum. The juggler was holding the villagers spell bound by his tricks. The simple minded villagers looked at him with open mouthed wonder and went almost delirious with joy at every new trick. To me, of course, most of the tricks appeared stale and dull but majority of the onlookers applauded him over and over again. Under the shade of a big tree children were enjoying themselves by riding the merry-go-round and by flying kites. In one corner I saw a gambling booth where the ignorant peasants wishing to make a little money, were being cheated of the little sum they had with them. I did not like it and muttering an oath and went on.

Evening came and the villagers soon began to disperse. All of them carried something or the other tied or wrapped in a piece of cloth hanging from their shoulders. I, too, bought some sweets for my younger brothers and made for my home.
